newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks end higher after volatile session.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks end higher after volatile session.

text.p: CHANGE CHANGE

* Toronto stocks ended higher on Friday, after a volatile session due to options expiry in New York * TSE gains in 9 of 14 sub-groups * 109 million shares traded worth C$1.75 billion
Toronto stocks closed higher on Friday, adding to Thursday's powerful rally after a volatile session due to options expiry on Wall Street.
The TSE 300 Composite Index rose 25.36 points to 5869.66 in brisk turnover of 109 million shares worth C$1.75 billion.
Advancing stocks outnumbered declines 567 to 421 with 297 issues unchanged. Analysts attributed the heavy trading volume to the expiry of options, futures and options on futures.
The TSE surged at the opening of today's session, but surrendered most of its gains by midday before resuming its climb in the afternoon.

The key 300 Index soared 116 points on Thursday, the third-biggest net gain ever for Canada's largest equity market. Fred Ketchen, director of equity trading for ScotiaMcLeod Inc, said he expects further gains for the Canadian market in the near term.
"I would think the year end rally still hasn't run out of steam and I suspect we may see more of this, but on a scaled down level next week," Ketchen said.
Toronto's strong side was led by consumer products, conglomerates and transportation. The TSE suffered minor losses in banking, precious metals and retailing.

* Bre-X Minerals Ltd jumped 1.10 to 22 on 3.3 million shares, buoyed by comments from Bre-X officials that investors would not be disappointed with a joint venture to develop the rich Busang gold find with Barrick Gold Corp.
Barrick Gold fell 1.35 to 39.75 on 1.4 million shares.
* Avenor Inc was the top issue by volume, falling 0.25 to 19.75 on 6.1 million shares. Avenor earlier this week announced a proposed takeover of Repap Enterprises.
* Gulf Canada Ltd rose 0.40 to close at 10.30 after earlier hitting a 52-week high of 10.35. Gulf rose as terms of its bid for Clyde Petroleum were digested by investors.
